approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a population of scored molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations. It retains high-scoring survivors, generates a fresh surplus pool, and uses a Gaussian process over counts of local molecular environments to sample possible scores jointly and choose the evaluation batch. Its retained chemistry includes direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchanges, and its repaired identity admission keeps graphs and accepted feedback aligned. In the single-parent mutation route, it usually applies one successful mutation but sometimes chains two or three before exposing the final molecule to pool selection; repeated generation failures can also trigger longer recovery walks.
approach.novelty: Remove routine optional continuation after the first successful mutation call. When generation is progressing normally, the first checked mutation product becomes the proposal; the existing longer-walk recovery rule remains intact when its inherited saturation condition occurs. Crossover, its optional finishing mutation, aromatic nitrogen exchanges and the count-based joint posterior all remain active. Earlier siblings removed those other mechanisms or changed posterior allocation; none isolated routine mutation-chain continuation. This tests whether the extra unscored transformations still earn their allocation after the developed selector chooses among a large fresh pool.

hypothesis: Ablate optional multi-call continuation in ordinary single-parent mutation proposals by using one GraphOperators.mutate call whenever the inherited saturation floor is one, while preserving the Parent's full sampled-length and escalation rule when that floor exceeds one.

finding_summary.headline: Removing ordinary continuation cut mutation calls, but failed the final-score margin.
finding_summary.insights:
Giving the selector access to more first-mutation products did not preserve the developed search loop's final quality. The affected first products have real successes, but those successes do not establish that their omitted continuations were wasteful. The parent also obtained 52 parent beats and eighteen incumbent improvements from accepted multi-call products. Across the whole Child run, parent beats and incumbent improvements actually became more frequent while final scores fell. Those local improvement counts depend on the changing parents and search history, so they cannot substitute for endpoint quality.

A mutation-call bound is a weak chemical constraint. Much of the small increase in parent similarity comes from removing the less similar multi-call cohort; the remaining one-call products are close to the parent's existing one-call products. Ring closure and nitrogen relocation can still change molecular presentation substantially, and crossover can produce much larger rearrangements. The molecular assessment finds that useful aryl/amine and carbonyl frameworks remain available, alongside more strained small rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified configurations. In docking, small-ring incidence rose from nine to 680 proposals even though the strongest observed open-chain amine did not require that strain.

This result supports retaining ordinary continuation in this particular composition and panel, without establishing an optimal mutation depth or identifying which omitted molecules would have helped. Seed two improved all five endpoints, so the effect is not universal across trajectories. No recovery-walk opportunity was observed. Fewer calls also do not establish faster generation: the large total wall-time reduction is dominated by a long Parent oracle evaluation, and Child wall time is higher in the other two seeds.
finding_summary.results:
Ordinary single-parent proposals now made exactly one mutation call in all 41,858 attempts. The retained length draw requested two or three calls in 7,387 attempts, suppressing 8,595 requested continuations. Of the resulting first products, 6,975 entered pools and 506 reached accepted evaluation; 88 beat their generating parent and 31 improved the incumbent. Crossover, its finishing mutations, nitrogen exchanges and correlated posterior selection all remained active. No saturation recovery branch was exercised.

All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.574344 to 0.555164, a paired loss of 0.019180 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were -0.024068, -0.039845 and +0.006373. Population score dispersion increased from 0.012317 to 0.027680, and mean recorded AUC fell from 0.482560 to 0.438018. All five task means declined, with the largest losses in docking (-0.049788) and sitagliptin (-0.023491). The mechanism executed correctly; its non-inferiority prediction was falsified.

Total mutation calls fell from 62,704 to 54,089 and raw inner attempts from 78,045 to 67,702, with the same 69,600 pool entries and 4,350 accepted proposals. Accepted single-parent descendants were slightly closer to their parents: mean count-fingerprint similarity rose from 0.8885 to 0.9010 and exact core retention from 46.41% to 49.11%. Chemistry did not improve uniformly: nitrogen-halogen-containing proposals rose from 745 to 1,208 and proposals with three- or four-membered rings from 268 to 1,558, while peroxide-containing proposals fell from 236 to 56.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich carbonyl and amine families retain reactive N-halogen bonds, small constrained rings and oversized heterocycles
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read, and every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rates are 0.9644-0.9839 and aromatic-token rates are 0.9138-0.9828. The tiny fragments in the worst-molecule excerpts therefore represent a small low-score tail, not an absence of ring or aromatic chemistry in the overall output. Mean SMILES lengths range from 42.2 to 87.8. The main families are indole-like aryl amides, large repeated aza-carbonyl assemblies, aryl polyamines, fused nitrogen/carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Families differ across seeds, but the strongest excerpts usually cluster around closely related frameworks. Relative to parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the output retains those broad themes while changing the prevalence of reactive heteroatom bonds and small rings. Ordinary amides, ethers and amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl/N-Br bonds, imines, N-N/N-O connections, aziridines, and some unusually substituted sulfur. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish solution protonation, and substituted rings are frequently stereochemically unresolved. Size, small-ring and configuration counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES; the digest counters themselves are string-level presence readings. No new oracle scores, synthesis scores or conformational feasibility results were generated. The chemistry is questionable because of these local bonding and geometry issues, not because medicinal fragments are missing altogether.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 25 heavy atoms. The leading molecules contain 24-26 heavy atoms and combine an indole-like fused aromatic system with an aryl or pyridyl carboxamide, vinyl groups and methyl, methoxy, thioether or methylamino substituents. The highest observed example has both an N-chloro amide and a fluorinated ring nitrogen. Many other leaders have N-fluoro or N-bromo amides. A strong alternative contains an ordinary N-H amide linking a fused N/O ring framework to a methylpyridyl group. The weakest excerpt consists of tiny molecules such as an interhalogen, acetylene, short hydrocarbons and a small sulfur/oxygen ring. The main aromatic-amide scaffolds are recognizable chemistry, but direct halogenation of their nitrogens creates much less convincing stable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: N-halogen amides and fluorinated aromatic ring nitrogen are distinct reactive-bond concerns from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
Vinyl groups, thioethers and fused N/O connections complicate stability or synthesis in some variants.
Tiny hydrocarbon, interhalogen and heterocyclic fragments discard the useful larger molecular arrangement.
missing_features: The tiny low-score fragments lack the assembled aromatic/carbonyl framework of the stronger compounds.

A complete set of conventional N-H amide and non-halogenated ring-nitrogen counterparts around the leading substituted core is not demonstrated. Existing ordinary amides show that reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds are not the only route to a nearby score.
The nitrogen-positional comparisons are uneven: some isomers tie while another pair differs, leaving attachment-specific donor/acceptor placement incompletely covered.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The doubly N-halogenated indole-like molecule scores 0.44941366017785356. Two ordinary N-H amide relatives differing in pyridine-nitrogen position both score 0.4451945621839941. Stable amide chemistry is therefore compatible with a nearby score, though these are not otherwise identical to the N-halogenated maximum. Matched N-fluoro/N-chloro amide variants share 0.436818201428663, as do N-fluoro/N-bromo variants in another substitution pattern. Those exact ties do not distinguish the different reactive halogen bonds. A separate pyridine-nitrogen positional pair scores 0.4387992465191 and 0.42762099872850584, showing that nitrogen placement can matter in a different local context. The tiny excerpt molecules score 0.0; the initial ordinary indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. The parent has the same indole/aryl-amide theme. Current per-seed maxima are 0.4451945621839941, 0.4239904333396317 and 0.44941366017785356, versus parental 0.45766047024715, 0.4423126980074005 and 0.4484138510190879. N-halogen-containing proposals increase from 102 to 312, so the current molecular set does not resolve that liability.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest and most elaborated output families: the median proposal has 46 heavy atoms versus 41 in the parent, and current examples reach 102. The strongest excerpt contains a pyridyl/phenyl unit, a branched unsaturated carbon chain, and repeated fused nitrogen-rich dione blocks joined through amino and exocyclic carbon-carbon unsaturated connections. The highest observed molecule has 50 heavy atoms. Closely related structures change polyene length or saturation, add fluorine or aldehyde, or add an unsaturated sulfur-fluoride side chain. Other seeds reach large fused carbonyl/thiocarbonyl heterocycles with N-halogen and N-O functionality. The low excerpt contains single-heavy-atom or other very small fragments. Familiar carbonyl and aza-aromatic groups are present, but duplicated complex blocks, extensive unsaturation and reactive heteroatom bonds make the assembled molecules difficult synthetic and stability propositions.
liabilities: Repeated heterocyclic units and large branched unsaturated chains increase size and assembly complexity.
Nitrogen-rich carbonyl blocks, exocyclic double bonds and polyenes introduce configuration and stability questions.
Sulfur-fluoride side chains and N-halogen/N-O groups elsewhere in the trajectories are chemically distinct liabilities; their presence is not justified by the local score ties.
missing_features: The small fragments lack the complete aromatic/aza-carbonyl organization retained by stronger molecules.
Compact alternatives retaining the same polar-group arrangement without repeated fused blocks and long unsaturated appendages remain incomplete.
Polyene and exocyclic double-bond geometry is unspecified, and no accessible geometry or stability is demonstrated for the highly elaborated assemblies.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading repeated-dione assembly scores 0.6182072829131653. Several relatives share exactly 0.6175345855359352 despite shortening, extending, saturating or moving bonds within the peripheral hydrocarbon chain. Fluorinated polyene relatives share 0.6180358829084042. A sulfur-fluoride-containing extension scores 0.6158894930521228. These observations associate the retained heterocyclic assembly with stronger scores more clearly than the exact chain elaboration; they do not demonstrate a requirement for its reactive terminal sulfur bond. The initial aromatic dione scores 0.548381482770623, while tiny fragments score 0.5. These are observed score levels, not proof that increasing molecular size is generally beneficial. The current seed-2 maximum 0.6182072829131653 is near parental 0.616992140985949 but uses a much more repeated heterocyclic arrangement than the parental seed-2 leader. Current seed-0 and seed-1 maxima are 0.5963296615082727 and 0.602363092888162, versus parental 0.6092799188640974 and 0.6199818405862896. The median size increase therefore does not correspond to a uniform improvement in the observed chemical families.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 35 heavy atoms versus 31 in the parent, although the strongest displayed compounds contain 25-31. They combine chlorinated aryl groups with accessible aliphatic amines and sometimes phenol or methoxy groups. The highest observed molecule is comparatively open-chain: a tertiary amine links arylalkyl groups and a side chain ending in an imine. Other leaders contain aziridine-linked polyamines or strongly fused/bridged nitrogen rings. The low examples include acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives, simple chlorinated arenes and a dialkyl peroxide; they lack the same assembled aryl/amine organization. Small-ring chemistry changes markedly relative to the parent: RDKit detects a three- or four-membered ring in 680 current proposals versus 9 parent proposals. The aryl/amine fragments are familiar, but aziridines, tight ring junctions and undefined configurations materially weaken the plausibility of many full molecules.
liabilities: Aziridines and tightly fused nitrogen rings introduce strain and potential reactivity.
The highest-scoring open-chain compound still contains an imine and an unassigned tetrahedral centre.
Multiple basic centres, chlorinated aryl surface and occasional unusual sulfur bonding occur together without demonstrated solution-state or conformational behavior.

The leading molecules combine an alkyl-substituted aryl group, an ethoxy-substituted aryl ether ring, and a fused nitrogen ring system containing two carbonyls and N-methyl groups. The highest observed structure has 35 heavy atoms and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. Dense fused and bridged rings impose geometric and synthetic demands.
The leading saturated ring junctions and substituted carbon sites have no assigned stereochemistry.

The leading excerpt does not establish a need for the extra N-N links or ring expansion. A fuller set of conventional, less labile connections retaining the same framework remains incomplete.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading families contain N-F, N-Cl and N-Br amides or ring nitrogens, and an elaborated high-score heterocycle has a sulfur-fluoride extension. Ordinary N-H amide isomers nevertheless reach 0.4451945621839941, close to the reactive-family maximum 0.44941366017785356. N-fluoro/N-chloro and N-fluoro/N-bromo pairs can share exactly 0.436818201428663.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator repeatedly attaches reactive nitrogen-halogen or related heteroatom bonds to otherwise useful aromatic/carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched conventional nitrogen and stable-linker alternatives while preserving useful ring and polar-group placement. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from N-, O- or S-halogen bonds and use chemically appropriate atom environments rather than treating all substitution sites as interchangeable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One panel contains 680 proposals with a three- or four-membered ring versus 9 in the parent. Its aziridine/polyamine leaders score up to 0.9882868043166894, while a simpler open-chain aryl tertiary amine reaches 0.9929316871171222. In a separate carbonyl-ring family, inserting an extra nitrogen lowers 0.2395559587801092 to 0.2347060970536737.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output frequently couples useful aryl/amine arrangements to small strained nitrogen rings while conventional counterparts remain incomplete.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ordinary-ring and open-chain alternatives accessible that preserve the useful amine or carbonyl spacing. Consider ring size, junction geometry and local bonding when changing topology, rather than equating extra ring closure or nitrogen insertion with improved molecular presentation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The largest leading family contains repeated fused dione blocks and a branched unsaturated chain; its top molecule has 50 heavy atoms. Multiple chain-length and saturation variants share 0.6175345855359352. A separate 56-heavy-atom linked aromatic/carbonyl assembly scores 3.7589249668299926e-42 despite containing many familiar fragments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular elaboration can duplicate heterocyclic blocks or extend unsaturated chains without a demonstrated local benefit.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include coherent contractions, removal of duplicated units and shorter stable linkers that retain the main attachment and polar-group pattern. Use actual feedback to establish whether additional molecular size or unsaturation contributes before continuing elaboration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Worst-molecule excerpts include single-heavy-atom species, acetylene, an interhalogen and small sulfur fragments. Several panels assign such fragments 0.0 or near-zero scores, while the corresponding stronger examples retain connected aromatic and polar frameworks. High overall ring-token rates show this is a small tail rather than the dominant output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output includes nearly atomic or very small reactive fragments that omit the larger molecular framework.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve a chemically meaningful connected fragment arrangement during contraction and recombination, while still allowing bounded size reduction. Distinguish a simpler complete scaffold from a fragment that has lost the structural context associated with useful feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every stereocentre-token and charged-token rate is 0.0. The leading fused dicarbonyl structure has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, the leading open-chain aryl amine has one, and the leading fluorinated imino heterocycle has one. Polyene and imino configurations are also omitted from the cited strings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify feasible stereochemical and molecular-state identities for constrained or imino-rich products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible configurations when changing substituted rings, junctions and unsaturated linkers. Track appropriate tautomer and protonation alternatives for imino heterocycles and basic amines; successful graph parsing does not establish an accessible stereoisomer or solution-state identity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Removing ordinary continuation cut mutation calls, but failed the final-score margin.
finding_summary.insights:
Giving the selector access to more first-mutation products did not preserve the developed search loop's final quality. The affected first products have real successes, but those successes do not establish that their omitted continuations were wasteful. The parent also obtained 52 parent beats and eighteen incumbent improvements from accepted multi-call products. Across the whole Child run, parent beats and incumbent improvements actually became more frequent while final scores fell. Those local improvement counts depend on the changing parents and search history, so they cannot substitute for endpoint quality.

A mutation-call bound is a weak chemical constraint. Much of the small increase in parent similarity comes from removing the less similar multi-call cohort; the remaining one-call products are close to the parent's existing one-call products. Ring closure and nitrogen relocation can still change molecular presentation substantially, and crossover can produce much larger rearrangements. The molecular assessment finds that useful aryl/amine and carbonyl frameworks remain available, alongside more strained small rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified configurations. In docking, small-ring incidence rose from nine to 680 proposals even though the strongest observed open-chain amine did not require that strain.

This result supports retaining ordinary continuation in this particular composition and panel, without establishing an optimal mutation depth or identifying which omitted molecules would have helped. Seed two improved all five endpoints, so the effect is not universal across trajectories. No recovery-walk opportunity was observed. Fewer calls also do not establish faster generation: the large total wall-time reduction is dominated by a long Parent oracle evaluation, and Child wall time is higher in the other two seeds.

finding_summary.headline: Removing ordinary continuation cut mutation calls, but failed the final-score margin.
finding_summary.insights:
Giving the selector access to more first-mutation products did not preserve the developed search loop's final quality. The affected first products have real successes, but those successes do not establish that their omitted continuations were wasteful. The parent also obtained 52 parent beats and eighteen incumbent improvements from accepted multi-call products. Across the whole Child run, parent beats and incumbent improvements actually became more frequent while final scores fell. Those local improvement counts depend on the changing parents and search history, so they cannot substitute for endpoint quality.

A mutation-call bound is a weak chemical constraint. Much of the small increase in parent similarity comes from removing the less similar multi-call cohort; the remaining one-call products are close to the parent's existing one-call products. Ring closure and nitrogen relocation can still change molecular presentation substantially, and crossover can produce much larger rearrangements. The molecular assessment finds that useful aryl/amine and carbonyl frameworks remain available, alongside more strained small rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified configurations. In docking, small-ring incidence rose from nine to 680 proposals even though the strongest observed open-chain amine did not require that strain.

This result supports retaining ordinary continuation in this particular composition and panel, without establishing an optimal mutation depth or identifying which omitted molecules would have helped. Seed two improved all five endpoints, so the effect is not universal across trajectories. No recovery-walk opportunity was observed. Fewer calls also do not establish faster generation: the large total wall-time reduction is dominated by a long Parent oracle evaluation, and Child wall time is higher in the other two seeds.

The parent also obtained 52 parent beats and eighteen incumbent improvements from accepted multi-call products. Across the whole Child run, parent beats and incumbent improvements actually became more frequent while final scores fell. Those local improvement counts depend on the changing parents and search history, so they cannot substitute for endpoint quality.

A mutation-call bound is a weak chemical constraint. Much of the small increase in parent similarity comes from removing the less similar multi-call cohort; the remaining one-call products are close to the parent's existing one-call products. Ring closure and nitrogen relocation can still change molecular presentation substantially, and crossover can produce much larger rearrangements. The molecular assessment finds that useful aryl/amine and carbonyl frameworks remain available, alongside more strained small rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified configurations. In docking, small-ring incidence rose from nine to 680 proposals even though the strongest observed open-chain amine did not require that strain.

This result supports retaining ordinary continuation in this particular composition and panel, without establishing an optimal mutation depth or identifying which omitted molecules would have helped. Seed two improved all five endpoints, so the effect is not universal across trajectories. No recovery-walk opportunity was observed. Fewer calls also do not establish faster generation: the large total wall-time reduction is dominated by a long Parent oracle evaluation, and Child wall time is higher in the other two seeds.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich carbonyl and amine families retain reactive N-halogen bonds, small constrained rings and oversized heterocycles
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read, and every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rates are 0.9644-0.9839 and aromatic-token rates are 0.9138-0.9828. The tiny fragments in the worst-molecule excerpts therefore represent a small low-score tail, not an absence of ring or aromatic chemistry in the overall output. Mean SMILES lengths range from 42.2 to 87.8. The main families are indole-like aryl amides, large repeated aza-carbonyl assemblies, aryl polyamines, fused nitrogen/carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Families differ across seeds, but the strongest excerpts usually cluster around closely related frameworks. Relative to parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the output retains those broad themes while changing the prevalence of reactive heteroatom bonds and small rings. Ordinary amides, ethers and amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl/N-Br bonds, imines, N-N/N-O connections, aziridines, and some unusually substituted sulfur. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish solution protonation, and substituted rings are frequently stereochemically unresolved. Size, small-ring and configuration counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES; the digest counters themselves are string-level presence readings. No new oracle scores, synthesis scores or conformational feasibility results were generated. The chemistry is questionable because of these local bonding and geometry issues, not because medicinal fragments are missing altogether.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 25 heavy atoms. The leading molecules contain 24-26 heavy atoms and combine an indole-like fused aromatic system with an aryl or pyridyl carboxamide, vinyl groups and methyl, methoxy, thioether or methylamino substituents. The highest observed example has both an N-chloro amide and a fluorinated ring nitrogen. Many other leaders have N-fluoro or N-bromo amides. A strong alternative contains an ordinary N-H amide linking a fused N/O ring framework to a methylpyridyl group. The weakest excerpt consists of tiny molecules such as an interhalogen, acetylene, short hydrocarbons and a small sulfur/oxygen ring. The main aromatic-amide scaffolds are recognizable chemistry, but direct halogenation of their nitrogens creates much less convincing stable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: N-halogen amides and fluorinated aromatic ring nitrogen are distinct reactive-bond concerns from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
Vinyl groups, thioethers and fused N/O connections complicate stability or synthesis in some variants.
Tiny hydrocarbon, interhalogen and heterocyclic fragments discard the useful larger molecular arrangement.
missing_features: The tiny low-score fragments lack the assembled aromatic/carbonyl framework of the stronger compounds.

A complete set of conventional N-H amide and non-halogenated ring-nitrogen counterparts around the leading substituted core is not demonstrated. Existing ordinary amides show that reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds are not the only route to a nearby score.
The nitrogen-positional comparisons are uneven: some isomers tie while another pair differs, leaving attachment-specific donor/acceptor placement incompletely covered.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a population of scored molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations. It retains high-scoring survivors, generates a fresh surplus pool, and uses a Gaussian process over counts of local molecular environments to sample possible scores jointly and choose the evaluation batch. Its retained chemistry includes direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchanges, and its repaired identity admission keeps graphs and accepted feedback aligned. In the single-parent mutation route, it usually applies one successful mutation but sometimes chains two or three before exposing the final molecule to pool selection; repeated generation failures can also trigger longer recovery walks.
approach.novelty: Remove routine optional continuation after the first successful mutation call. When generation is progressing normally, the first checked mutation product becomes the proposal; the existing longer-walk recovery rule remains intact when its inherited saturation condition occurs. Crossover, its optional finishing mutation, aromatic nitrogen exchanges and the count-based joint posterior all remain active. Earlier siblings removed those other mechanisms or changed posterior allocation; none isolated routine mutation-chain continuation. This tests whether the extra unscored transformations still earn their allocation after the developed selector chooses among a large fresh pool.
